profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a Bolivian public-interest law NGO preparing a joint evidence package for residents in a peri-urban settlement claimed by both La Paz and Palca, where overlapping municipal enforcement has produced duplicate tax demands, contradictory building notices, and conflicting service commitments. The immediate trigger is a new round of inspections expected next week and an internal deadline to assemble Friday's shared bundle for use across the litigation and field-documentation workstreams. The agenda is to align on what goes into each resident packet, which map exhibit will anchor the territorial narrative, how the shared 'case file' should be maintained, and when materials are ready to move into the final folder. The expected outcome is a clean handoff plan so both teams believe they have synchronized inputs for the same resident set without revisiting basic terminology.

members.name: Valeria Quiroga
members.role: Senior Staff Attorney, Constitutional and Administrative Litigation
members.expertise: Constitutional remedies, municipal competence disputes, evidentiary annexing for urgent filings
members.background: Valeria trained in La Paz, clerked at a constitutional chamber, and now leads strategic litigation challenging overlapping municipal enforcement actions affecting peri-urban settlements.
members.private_state: She wants Friday's bundle to be immediately usable for drafting and annex numbering without later having to strip out materials that look informal, duplicative, or weakly attributable to a specific parcel, because she expects any inconsistency to be exploited by municipal counsel.
hidden_assumptions: When colleagues say 'the case file,' they mean the curated evidentiary set for the agreed resident households, not the broader working dossier that may contain raw notes or backup material.
The relevant 'latest map' is the most recent georeferenced boundary exhibit already normalized for legal use, unless someone expressly distinguishes it from community sketches.

A packet is 'complete' once the required categories are present in a form suitable for legal reliance, meaning legible copies that can be cited and, where needed, later formalized without changing the substance.
Anything placed in the 'final folder' is effectively frozen except for litigation-side renaming, ordering, or conversion into annex format.

members.name: Diego Mamani
members.role: Community Legal Coordinator, Field Documentation and Resident Liaison
members.expertise: Resident intake, neighborhood organization records, municipal paperwork collection, coordination with settlement leaders
members.background: Diego grew up in El Alto, has spent years supporting peri-urban resident committees, and now manages field intake processes and evidence gathering across disputed fringe territories.
members.private_state: He wants residents' documentation efforts to count even when formal paperwork is patchy, and he is trying to preserve momentum with settlement leaders by making sure the legal team works from the fullest possible household record rather than sending requests back for perfection.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the case file,' they mean the full working dossier for those same agreed resident households, including photos, interview notes, leader certifications, and informal backup that may later support legal or organizing decisions.
The operative 'latest map' is whichever current territorial depiction best reflects where inspections, service collections, and neighborhood boundaries are being enforced on the ground this week.

A packet is 'complete' when the required categories have been substantively covered for handoff, even if the evidence arrives as phone photos, neighborhood receipts, or uncertified scans that can later be upgraded.
The 'final folder' is the current shared workspace for the live set everyone is coordinating from, so improved scans or updated certifications should continue replacing earlier versions there.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to organizing the resident 'case file' for Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the curated legal-use file for the already agreed households: only materials she expects to cite, annex, or rely on in drafting, with raw notes and duplicative photos kept outside that file.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the comprehensive working file for those same households: the formal documents plus interview notes, site photos, neighborhood leader letters, WhatsApp screenshots, and other contextual material collected in intake.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are talking about the same households and the same deadline, the phrase sounds fully aligned; the hidden divergence is only about the internal contents of a routine legal folder, which each sees as obvious from normal practice.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'latest map' will anchor the packet
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the bundle should include 'the latest map' of the disputed zone.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the georeferenced municipal delineation exhibit updated from prior jurisdiction briefs and suitable for attachment in a filing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the neighborhood federation's recently revised sector map showing current inspection routes, service points, and the boundary as residents are experiencing it.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each has one salient map in current use and both treat it as the obvious latest version; since the meeting is about coordination rather than substantive territorial argument, neither naturally specifies the exact artifact.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree Diego will hand off 'complete' resident packets in batches.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'complete' means the packet contains the needed categories in legally reliable form for drafting—e.g., legible ID copies, a possession or purchase document that can be attributed to the resident, and municipal acts clear enough to quote or annex without ambiguity.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'complete' means the packet contains those same categories in practically sufficient form for legal review—e.g., smartphone photos of IDs, neighborhood purchase receipts, handwritten possession attestations, and informal scans that establish the story even if not yet polished.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the categories of material, so the conversation sounds precise; the unnoticed gap is the evidentiary threshold for what counts as having that category 'present,' a second-order standard that usually stays implicit.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to keep materials in the 'final folder' so everyone is working from the same set.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the final folder is a controlled repository whose contents are substantively stable once uploaded, with subsequent changes limited to litigation-side formatting or file naming.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the final folder is the main live folder for the current best version, so field staff should continue swapping in cleaner scans, revised certifications, and better photos as they arrive.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Shared-drive etiquette is rarely articulated because both conventions are locally normal; since both are trying to reduce version confusion, the same phrase masks opposite assumptions about whether files there are frozen or still evolving.
